rationale: Only the Entry Motion sensor is offline while all 6 other devices are online, ruling out a base-station or batch fault. The device shows strong RSSI (-60 dBm), 75% battery, and compatible firmware (v3), yet remains offline even next to the base station after a reset. The customer dropped it on tiles while changing the battery, and the escalation policy explicitly requires L2 escalation when a device fails next to the base station after a reset — consistent with physical/hardware damage.

results.text: HB-100 owner could not add a new door sensor; app showed E-201. Base station already had 8 devices. Customer removed an old test sensor and pairing succeeded. Resolved at frontline.

Escalate when any of the following holds: (1) two or more peripherals fail at the same time while the base station is online; (2) a firmware or protocol mismatch remains after an OTA attempt or OTA is not possible; (3) the standard frontline fix was executed and the problem persists; (4) the app's device list and the base station binding table disagree; (5) a device fails even next to the base station after a factory reset.
Logged by the base station when its sub-GHz radio fails self-test or multiple peripherals drop simultaneously. Always escalate to FAE.
